content:
Want to use Signal on multiple devices at the same time? This encrypted messaging service now makes it easier for users to use the app across iPhones and other devices.

Signal users can now link another iPhone to their existing Signal account, instead of being limited to using iPads as secondary mobile devices.

The company also announced support for Android linking today, stating: "We are expanding linked device support on iOS, allowing you to link an iPhone to your Signal account, and our support for iPad will continue."

When linking another iPhone, users can choose whether to transfer their complete message history, as well as media files saved in the past 45 days.

Signal said the transfer process uses the same "link-and-sync" technology as iPads and desktop devices (including Signal for Mac), with end-to-end encryption throughout.

This expanded support is particularly useful for users who need to keep work and personal iPhones separate, or for those who need to test multiple devices.

This move also brings Signal's multi-device experience closer to Apple's Messages ecosystem, enabling seamless conversations across iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

Signal iOS version 8.22 is now available on the App Store. Signal has also previously introduced a username feature, allowing users to contact each other without sharing phone numbers.
